question: Why was a 1949 two-car convoy chosen for the world's first solar train?
answer: Australia didn't build a new vehicle. In 2017 it converted a two-car convoy from 1949 into a solar train. Reusing it skipped the cost and time of a new train and showed that old trains can also go solar.
move: Converting what already runs is cheaper and faster than building new.
